title: SLO Sensitivity & Capacity Sentinel Playbook
author: Aisha Patel
content:
Overview
========

This playbook defines the SLO Sensitivity and Capacity Sentinel pattern used by Redwood to proactively detect SLO regressions that are driven by capacity, workload composition, or sudden sensitivity of model-serving paths (e.g., quantized vs full-precision kernels, KV cache miss storms). The Capacity Sentinel is a lightweight, autoscaling-aware decision agent that correlates SLO signal changes with capacity/serving state and triggers controlled mitigations.

Motivation
----------
- Model-serving SLOs (latency, availability, token-completion quality) can degrade for reasons that are operational (capacity, scheduling, OOMs) or model-related (regression after model rollout). Distinguishing cause quickly reduces mean time to mitigation and avoids unnecessary rollbacks.
- Automated, conservative mitigations (prefix throttles, model variant fallback, burst capacity lift) restore surface-level SLOs while preserving investigation time.

Scope
-----
Applies to all inference clusters backing the Redwood Hosted API and Dedicated pools. Exclusions: on-prem private deployments where customer policy prohibits autoscaling; those deployments must use the sentinel as guidance only.

Ownership
---------
- SLO Owner: eng-sre (primary action owner)
- Runtime/Serving Owner: eng-serving-runtime (responsible for model variant toggles and kernel fallbacks)
- Observability/Tooling Owner: eng-platform (dashboards, alerting rules)
- Oncall: model-serving-oncall (first responder for sentinel escalations)

High-level workflow
-------------------
1. Telemetry agents produce SLO windows (5m, 1h) for latency p50/p95/p99, tail token latency, correctness regressions (quality evals).
2. Capacity Sentinel correlates SLO windows with: GPU utilization, pending queue depth, autoscaler decisions, KV cache miss rate, and recent model rollout tags.
3. If correlation crosses a configured sensitivity threshold, Sentinel runs a mitigation policy (graded, reversible).
4. Sentinel creates an incident with diagnostic evidence and a hypothesis tag (capacity|model|infra).
5. Oncall follows the runbook; if hypothesis is model-related, serving runtime triggers canary rollback. If capacity-related, follow capacity remediation steps.

Signals and thresholds
----------------------
Primary signals (examples):
- latency_p95_ms (5m): > 1200 ms -> signal high
- latency_p99_ms (5m): > 1800 ms -> signal critical
- request_error_rate (5m): > 0.5% absolute increase and > 0.2% baseline -> signal medium
- gpu_utilization (cluster, 1m): > 85% for 5m -> capacity-pressure
- queue_depth (per-pool, 1m): > 200 requests -> capacity-pressure
- kv_cache_miss_rate (rolling 10m): > 30% and increasing -> cache-eviction storm
- recent_deploy_tag (metadata): rollout_fraction > 10% in last 15m -> suspect-deploy

Sensitivity correlation heuristic (implemented by Sentinel):
- If (latency_p95 degrade) && (gpu_utilization > 80% OR queue_depth > threshold) -> probable capacity
- If (latency degrade) && (recent_deploy_tag present) && (gpu_utilization < 60%) -> probable model regression
- If (kv_cache_miss_rate spike) && (latency tail increase) -> cache storm -> partial mitigation: prefetched-prefix warming

Mitigation tiers (automated, safe-by-default)
--------------------------------------------
1) Tier 1 — Soft throttle and cache warm: prefix-based admission control (new requests throttled to 70% of usual), prewarm KV cache for high-volume keys. No model changes.
2) Tier 2 — Autoscaler soft-lift: temporarily increase desired capacity by up to 20% for the pool with a 15-minute cool-down. If cloud spend budget disallows, fall back to tier 1.
3) Tier 3 — Model variant fallback: route 30% of traffic to a lower-latency/quantized variant with validated quality guardrails. Triggered only when correlation indicates model-serving path sensitivity and after operator approval when possible.
4) Tier 4 — Canary rollback: automatic only if rollback-safe flag is set on the rollout. Otherwise create incident and require manual rollback.

Runbook: immediate steps for oncall (first 30 minutes)
----------------------------------------------------
1. Acknowledge Sentinel incident and check hypothesis tag. Collect the following evidence links and paste into incident:
   - Grafana dashboard: "SLO Sentinels / {pool}" (link)
   - Prometheus query snapshots (see samples below)
   - Last 30m of autoscaler events: /internal/autoscaler/events/{pool}
2. Verify scope: is degradation localized to single pool / region / model?
   - Use query: sum by (pool_id) (increase(requests_failed_total[10m]))
3. Correlate with capacity metrics: GPU utilization, pending queue, OOM events.
4. If hypothesis == capacity AND gpu_utilization > 85%: execute Tier 2. Run: 
   - CLI (internal): rwdctl capacity bump --pool {pool_id} --pct 20 --duration 15m --owner "oncall"
5. If hypothesis == cache_storm: execute Tier 1 and initiate cache prewarm: 
   - Sample prewarm script (described): call /internal/kvcache/prewarm with top-keys list from Telemetry.
6. If hypothesis == model_regression AND rollback-safe: execute Tier 4 rollback: 
   - rwdctl rollout rollback --model {model_id} --to-version {previous_version} --reason "SLOSentinelAutoRollback"
7. If mitigation restored SLO window within 15 minutes, mark incident as mitigated and start investigation ticket for root cause. If not restored after Tier 3, escalate to eng-serving-runtime and oncall lead.

Prometheus/Grafana examples
---------------------------
Prometheus sample alerts (text):
- AlertRule: SLO_Sentinel_Latency_P95_High
  Expr: histogram_quantile(0.95, sum(rate(request_duration_seconds_bucket[5m])) by (le, service)) * 1000 > 1200
  For: 5m
  Labels: severity=page, hypothesis=latency

- AlertRule: SLO_Sentinel_GPU_Overload
  Expr: avg by (pool) (gpu_utilization_percent) > 85
  For: 5m
  Labels: severity=page, hypothesis=capacity

Note: alerts must contain hypothesis label and pool_id for the sentinel to attach evidence automatically.

Capacity Sentinel configuration (YAML example)
-------------------------------------------
# sentinel-config.yaml (simplified)
sentinel_name: slo-sensitivity-1
signal_windows: ["5m","1h"]
correlation_rules:
  - name: capacity_pressure
    conditions: ["latency_p95 > 1200","gpu_utilization > 80"]
    mitigation: tier2
  - name: cache_storm
    conditions: ["kv_cache_miss_rate > 30","latency_p99 > 1800"]
    mitigation: tier1
mitigations:
  tier1: { action: "throttle_prefix:70", reversible: true }
  tier2: { action: "autoscale_bump:20", reversible: true }
  tier3: { action: "route_variant:quantized-30pct", reversible: true }
  tier4: { action: "rollback_canary", reversible: false }

Investigation checklist (post-mitigation)
-----------------------------------------
- Collect and preserve telemetry windows (export to incident evidence store).
- Validate whether a model rollout was correlated (tagged deploys in last 30m).
- If capacity: evaluate whether autoscaler policy needs adjustment (scale sensitivity or upper/lower bounds).
- If model: run quick-run of evaluation harness against saved prompt-sets to detect quality regressions.
- Create follow-up Jira ticket with: root_cause_hypothesis, mitigation_taken, time_to_mitigate, suggested action (tuning/infra/model).

SLO & error budget guidance (practical notes)
-------------------------------------------
- Prefer SLO windows that align with user experience: for generation endpoints use p95 token-latency and completion success rate. For embeddings use 99th percentile tail latency.
- Track both absolute SLO breaches and rate-of-change (delta) to detect sudden sensitivity. A 30% relative jump in p95 over 10 minutes is considered a high-sensitivity event.
- Maintain a 24/7 error budget reserve for emergency autoscale lifts; this is consumed before billing exceptions and must be reconciled weekly.

Operational tooling integration checklist
--------------------------------------
- Ensure alerts include hypothesis labels and pool_id.
- Dashboards: create per-pool SLO Sentinels panel set and an executive SLO-sensitivity heatmap.
- Incident automation: sentinel should attach snapshot links and issue templates automatically.
- Simulation: use the stress harness in eng-serving-runtime to rehearse sentinel triggers quarterly.

Fallout and rollback policy
--------------------------
- All automated mitigations are tagged with a reversible flag. Tier 4 rollback is non-reversible and requires additional guardrails (canary safety flag).
- Any billing-impactful mitigation (autoscaler lift beyond reserved capacity) must include a human approval within 30 minutes or be automatically scaled back.

Metrics to track success of the playbook
--------------------------------------
- Median time to mitigation (target < 10m for Tier 1/2).
- Fraction of incidents where sentinel hypothesis matched postmortem root cause (target > 80%).
- Count of unnecessary rollbacks or rollbacks that were avoidable (target < 5% of rollbacks).
- Weekly spend from emergency autoscale budget.

---------------------------------
